title: Strategic customer impact allocator and timebound commitment scheduler
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Execs and sales consistently request timebound commitments for top accounts (deliver by X quarter) but engineering capacity is limited and current intake signals are noisy. We need a transparent mechanism to translate customer impact signals into prioritized, timeboxed commitments that product, sales, and engineering can rely on for planning.

Proposal: Build a lightweight "Impact Allocator" that scores inbound top-account asks across weighted dimensions (revenue at risk, strategic breadth, legal/regulatory urgency, integration complexity, renewal horizon). Pair the allocator with a "Timebound Commitment Scheduler" that converts score into one of three commitment tiers (Admit: runway + scope lock; Conditional: partial deliverable + advisory timeline; Advisory: signal recorded for backlog). The scheduler will include a compact SLA ledger for agreed dates and auto-expiry rules to avoid indefinite promises.

Goals: Reduce ambiguous roadmap promises, shorten executive negotiation cycles, increase predictability for eng resourcing, and create a verifiable audit trail for customer commitments.
success_criteria: Reduction in ad-hoc commitment requests requiring exec mediation by 60% within two cycles
>= 85% of accepted 'Admit' commitments met within agreed timebox or recorded exceptions
Sales and CS adoption: 90% of top-account intake goes through new allocator workflow
Engineering capacity planner can map allocated runway to sprint planning with <10% rework rate
acceptance_criteria: Allocator UI (Console) shows weighted score and recommended tier for each incoming ask
Scheduler creates a commitment record with immutable timestamp, owner, tier, and auto-expiry rules
Notifications to Sales/CS and Engineering on Admit/Conditional decisions with follow-up tasks created in Linear
Metrics emitted to Console: commitment lead time, fulfillment rate, SLA exceptions; dashboards validated in Grafana
PRD + small implementation spike merged and reviewed by PM, Eng lead, and Design

notes: We will pilot on 8 named strategic accounts from the enterprise book (list provided in Drive) before org-wide rollout

Weighting defaults: revenue_at_risk=30%, renewal_window=25%, regulatory_urgency=20%, integration_complexity=-10% (negative factor reduces score if high complexity), strategic_breadth=35% (cap to avoid over-weighting) - provisional
Commitment tiers: Admit (hard commitment, reserve runway), Conditional (partial milestone with advisory date), Advisory (signal + no commitment)
Auto-expiry rule: after 90 days without scheduled milestone, Commitment reverts to 'Advisory' and notification sent to account owner
Legal: any requests tagged 'regulatory' auto-create a legal review task and bump priority to P0 if within 30 days of compliance deadline

decisions: Adopt a hybrid scoring approach (numeric score + rule overrides) rather than pure threshold gating — enables manual override by PM with audit
Use three commitment tiers to simplify downstream resourcing and communication (Admit/Conditional/Advisory)
Pilot on a small cohort of accounts for 6 weeks before making thresholds global
Do not expose internal engineering runway estimates to customers; only expose tier and milestone dates
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales bypassing the allocator to get faster commitments -> Mitigation: require intake ticket for any commitment claims and enforce via AM incentives
Risk: Overfitting weights to current quarter -> Mitigation: schedule quarterly re-calibration with Finance and Sales Ops
Risk: Engineering capacity mismatch if many Admits accepted -> Mitigation: soft quota per cycle and emergency fallback policy (auto-offer Conditional)
Risk: Legal/regulatory commitments inadvertently promised -> Mitigation: auto-create legal review for flagged items and block Admit until completion
